numeric.proof_assessment: Separate blinded rubric required; numeric agreement is not a proof.

proof.rubric_amendment: freeze-amendment-001.json; value continuity and differentiability mandatory

blinding.limitation: Candidate prose itself was visible; it did not identify its treatment. This is one reviewer applying a predeclared rubric, not multiple independent human graders.

evidence.quote: The polygon is nonempty, closed, and bounded, so a minimum exists.

dimensions.observed_reason: The feasible polygon is correctly retained and its five vertices listed. Nonemptiness and compactness establish existence. The reduced Hessian has the correct positive leading minors 8 and 32; the equivalent positive quadratic remainder proves strict convexity and uniqueness on the equality plane.

evidence.quote: Intervals deliberately overlap at their endpoints

dimensions.observed_reason: The six exact optimizer formulas coincide with the independent reference. The five transitions -3/2,-1,-1/2,0,9/5 and the full closed domain are represented without gaps. The constant vertex interval [-1/2,0] is explicitly included and derived using its incident feasible directions.

All six exact value formulas are correct. In particular the shifted-square formula in B expands to 31/16-9t/4-3t^2/4, and C written as 4-(5+2t)^2/16 matches the reference. Transition and endpoint values are independently consistent. This is a symbolic assessment rather than an inference from numeric tests.

The reduced polygon includes every original constraint. The derivation gives explicit coordinate bounds for B, the lower-edge feasibility limit for C and the slanted-edge interval for E. Together with the closed table, these establish nonnegative coordinates, unit sum, the cap and slanted constraint; z>=3/10 is correctly stated throughout.

evidence.quote: Every multiplier not shown as nonzero is explicitly zero

dimensions.observed_reason: The original-variable Lagrangian and all three stationarity equations are correct. The table explicitly supplies the equality multiplier and all five inequality multipliers for every closed interval. Its equivalent reduced stationarity equations correctly recover the table, and direct symbolic substitution confirms every row.

evidence.quote: whether or not its multiplier is positive

dimensions.observed_reason: Complementarity is written explicitly and all inequality multipliers are nonnegative on their complete intervals. The D row supports both active constraints with multipliers -2t and 1+2t. Boundary active sets and vanishing multipliers are correct. The additional assertion that the listed active gradients plus the equality gradient are independent is also correct here.

evidence.quote: At each transition the adjacent optimizer, value, and multiplier formulas agree.
Thus \(V\) is continuously differentiable on the closed interval

dimensions.observed_reason: Each transition is derived from feasibility contact, directional derivative sign or multiplier support. Both vertex intervals are correctly justified. The explicit transition table agrees with adjoining optimizer, value and multiplier formulas. The six derivative formulas equal -2x*(t), have the correct shared values and are stated with one-sided outer-endpoint derivatives, satisfying the mandatory C1 requirement.

evidence.quote: These certificates prove global optimality directly
Consequently every distinct feasible competitor has strictly larger objective.

dimensions.observed_reason: For an arbitrary feasible competitor, affine constraints, nonnegative multipliers and complementary slackness give a nonnegative first-order gap. The exact strictly positive quadratic remainder establishes global optimality and uniqueness. The proof explicitly applies this to every polygon point and the six closed parameter intervals, so no competing face or real-parameter range is omitted.

proof.scope_limit: One parametric problem. Eight proof dimensions and repeated numeric probes do not constitute eight independent problems or evidence of broad model superiority.

processReview.summary: The second baseline math run followed a stated derive–implement–verify sequence and recorded successful numerical and import checks.

observations.observed: The public outline identified regime derivation, KKT multipliers, implementation and comparison with feasible-face enumeration before code was written.
The candidate wrote the solver and verification helper, executed the helper successfully and recorded the Python version. The helper includes local import and guarded module-execution checks.
A final command wrote the verification record, checked expected files and cleaned candidate-created bytecode. No mathematical check failure or corrective solver edit is recorded.

limits: The baseline already has native Codex process guidance.
The absence of a recorded failure does not prove that the first design was complete or optimal.
The numerical helper and accompanying proof require the separate independent acceptance review.
This descriptive process audit was requested after outcomes existed. It is retrospective and exploratory, not a preregistered process endpoint.
The methods reviewer knows condition assignments; this review is not blinded. Separate proof/design reviewers have their own blinding procedures.
Only public progress messages, observable tool actions, check exits and retained artifact evidence are summarized. No hidden reasoning is inferred or published.
There is no process score, tool-call leaderboard or causal claim. More messages, calls, checks or elapsed time do not imply a better process.
The baseline retains native Codex instructions and the same common trial directions. It is not an unstructured or instruction-free model.
Delegation, external services and auxiliary model calls were prohibited for both conditions. Full orchestration, provider selection, collaboration and autonomous end-to-end deployment are unmeasured.
Treatment includes three or four pinned contracts plus a repository snapshot. Observed behavior cannot be assigned to an individual Fabius rule from this design.
Candidate-authored tests and self-reported passes are process evidence, not substitutes for the independent acceptance and proof checks.
Coverage includes all 12 finalized valid runs from the planned three-task, two-condition, two-repeat study. The two preserved setup attempts are documented separately.
